description: RISK R-B, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE CLASS NAME INVERTS THE BEHAVIOUR: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN02C is TransactionViewController, but this program does not view - it ADDS. Two independent sources say so: app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 'Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and README.md:224 '| CT02 | COTRN02 | COTRN02C | Transaction Add |', which sits directly beneath README.md:223 '| CT01 | COTRN01 | COTRN01C | Transaction View |' - so the prompt's mapping is the inverse of the repository's own inventory and the mirror image of parity/COTRN01C, whose program genuinely views. Rule R1 governs the resolution - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and practice B4 governs the disclosure, so the divergence is documented here and never silently corrected; the Agent Action Plan escalates it for explicit user confirmation, and nothing here guesses which artefact is authoritative about intent, only about behaviour, where the source is the only oracle there is. No case in this folder is downgraded to read-only to match the name: the EXEC CICS WRITE at :713 is pinned at its full 350 bytes by case19 and case20. WHAT THIS CASE PINS, AND WHY IT TAKES FOUR STEPS TO GET THERE: the re-entered screen resolves its key through the CARD arm and is then rejected by the LAST arm of the eleven-arm empty cascade. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives at '1', so NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :120 is false, :132 receives the map and the ordered EVALUATE EIBAID at :133-152 takes its first arm, DFHENTER at :134, into PROCESS-ENTER-KEY. STEP 1 - ARM 2 OF VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS (:193-230), WHICH IS ONLY REACHABLE BECAUSE ARM 1 MISSES. The EVALUATE TRUE at :195 tests ACTIDINI first, at :196, and ACTIDINI arrives as eleven spaces here: the guard is the abbreviated combined relation NOT = SPACES AND LOW-VALUES, which a field of spaces does not satisfy, so arm 1 does not match and control reaches :210. Leaving the account field blank is therefore not incidental to this case, it is the whole precondition - and the asymmetry matters, because when BOTH keys are supplied arm 1 wins and :209 MOVE XREF-CARD-NUM TO CARDNINI OF COTRN2AI overwrites whatever card number the operator typed. Arm 2 at :210 matches on a sixteen-digit CARDNINI, and the class test at :211 IF CARDNINI IS NOT NUMERIC passes because every one of the sixteen positions is a digit, so the rejection at :212-216 is skipped. STEP 2 - THE CONVERSION AND THE RENORMALISATION. :218-219 COMPUTE WS-CARD-NUM-N = FUNCTION NUMVAL(CARDNINI OF COTRN2AI) converts into WS-CARD-NUM-N PIC 9(16) (:56), and :220-221 MOVE WS-CARD-NUM-N TO XREF-CARD-NUM and to CARDNINI OF COTRN2AI writes the converted value back over the screen field. That second receiver is the renormalisation: a PIC 9(16) source is zero-filled to its full width on the way out (rule R5), so the card number returns to the operator as sixteen zero-padded digits. For the value this case uses the pad is a NO-OP and is stated as such rather than left implicit - 0683586198171516 already occupies all sixteen positions and already begins with a zero, so the round trip through PIC 9(16) is byte-identical. Asserting it anyway is the point: a translation that trimmed the field, or that carried the number as a long and rendered it without padding, would drop that leading zero and the assertion would catch it. STEP 3 - READ-CCXREF-FILE (:609-637) ON THE BASE CLUSTER, RETURNING NORMAL. :222 performs it and it issues EXEC CICS READ DATASET(WS-CCXREF-FILE) INTO(CARD-XREF-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF CARD-XREF-RECORD) RIDFLD(XREF-CARD-NUM) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF XREF-CARD-NUM) RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD), then an ordered three-arm EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD whose arms and owners are: DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :622-623 CONTINUE, which is THIS case and the only case in this folder that drives it on the base cluster; DFHRESP(NOTFND) at :624-629, 'Card Number NOT found...' with MOVE -1 TO CARDNINL, which is case11 - it seeds the same five fixture rows and asks for 9999999999999999, a key none of them carries; and WHEN OTHER at :630-636, which DISPLAYs 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD and reports 'Unable to lookup Card # in XREF file...', a condition the source does not enumerate and that no seeded row can produce - it is driven by TransactionViewControllerTest.cardLookupFails rather than by a case here, and is named so that the arm's existence is recorded even though this folder does not reach it. (The brief for this file attributed NOTFND to case13 and WHEN OTHER to case14; the folder as built assigns case13 to the positional amount check and case14 to the positional origination-date check, so the owners are named from the folder rather than from the brief - practice B4.) TWO ACCESS PATHS, ONE CLUSTER, NEVER TWO TABLES (gate G45). This read is keyed on XREF-CARD-NUM against the BASE key-sequenced cluster: app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:37-39 defines FILE(CCXREF) with a DSNAME operand naming the card cross-reference VSAM KSDS - the name itself is not repeated here, because no fully-qualified mainframe dataset name appears anywhere in this file (gate G46). READ-CXACAIX-FILE at :576-604 reads the very same data through CXACAIX, which the CSD defines as an alternate-index PATH over that base and which is keyed on XREF-ACCT-ID instead - and case09, case10 and case13 all reach the cross-reference that way. So the pair of paths is exercised across the folder while exactly ONE dataset is ever seeded, which is what the gate is about: one repository per base cluster with a second finder for the alternate key, and no second table anywhere. The two finders are visible as such in the translation - CardXrefRepository.readByCardNumber against BASE_DD_NAME, and readByAccountIdViaAltIndex against ALTERNATE_INDEX_DD_NAME. THE ACTIDIN OVERWRITE. The read succeeds, so :223 MOVE XREF-ACCT-ID TO ACTIDINI OF COTRN2AI writes the account identifier the cross-reference carries over the field the operator left blank. The widths change on the way: XREF-ACCT-ID is PIC 9(11) in app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy and ACTIDINI is PIC X(11) in app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY, so eleven digits land in eleven positions exactly with no pad and no truncation. The row this case keys on is the SECOND of the five seeded, chosen deliberately: card 0683586198171516 resolves to account 00000000027, whereas case13 resolves the FIRST row's account 00000000050 to card 0500024453765740 through the alternate index. A keyed read that ignored its key and returned the first row it held would satisfy case13 and fail here, which is the assertion a first-row choice could not make. STEP 4 - ARM 11 OF THE ELEVEN-ARM EMPTY CASCADE, WHICH IS THIS CASE'S SUBJECT (gate G30). :167 performs VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS (:235). WS-ERR-FLG is still 'N' - nothing raised it, since every guard on the way here passed - so the IF ERR-FLG-ON block at :237-249 does NOT run and the ten populated detail fields survive into the EVALUATE. That block is worth naming even though it is skipped, because it carries a quirk of its own: it lists TRNAMTI before TDESCI while the EVALUATE below tests TDESC before TRNAMT, so the two orders genuinely differ and neither may be normalised to the other. The EVALUATE TRUE at :251 is an ordered, first-match-wins chain of ELEVEN arms followed by WHEN OTHER CONTINUE at :318-319, and all eleven are recorded here in source order with the text each reports and the xxxL item each moves -1 into: (1) :252 TTYPCDI - 'Type CD can NOT be empty...' - TTYPCDL; (2) :258 TCATCDI - 'Category CD can NOT be empty...' - TCATCDL; (3) :264 TRNSRCI - 'Source can NOT be empty...' - TRNSRCL; (4) :270 TDESCI - 'Description can NOT be empty...' - TDESCL; (5) :276 TRNAMTI - 'Amount can NOT be empty...' - TRNAMTL; (6) :282 TORIGDTI - 'Orig Date can NOT be empty...' - TORIGDTL; (7) :288 TPROCDTI - 'Proc Date can NOT be empty...' - TPROCDTL; (8) :294 MIDI - 'Merchant ID can NOT be empty...' - MIDL; (9) :300 MNAMEI - 'Merchant Name can NOT be empty...' - MNAMEL; (10) :306 MCITYI - 'Merchant City can NOT be empty...' - MCITYL; and (11) :312-317 MZIPI - 'Merchant Zip can NOT be empty...' - MZIPL, which is the arm this case drives. Reaching the ELEVENTH arm requires all ten fields before it to be populated and only MZIPI blank, which is exactly how the request below is built, and that is what makes this case the folder's proof that the chain is strictly ordered and that its final arm is reachable at all rather than shadowed by an earlier one. Arm 1 is driven by case03, reached from the first-entry path that also processes a selection; arms 2 to 10 are recorded above and driven by TransactionViewControllerTest.theEmptyCascade, whose @CsvSource lists all eleven in this same order - a parity folder capped at twenty cases (gate G15) cannot spend eleven of them on one cascade, and no extra file is created for them. THE TASK ENDS INSIDE THE GUARD, WHICH IS WHY EXACTLY ONE MESSAGE IS REPORTED AND NOTHING IS WRITTEN. :317 performs SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN (:516-534), which populates the header, moves WS-MESSAGE to ERRMSGO and sends the map - and then executes EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) at :530-534. That RETURN ends the CICS task, so control never comes back to the statement after the PERFORM: the numeric edits at :322-337, the positional shape edits from :339, the CSUTLDTC calls at :393 and :413, and above all the EVALUATE CONFIRMI at :169 are all UNREACHED. This case makes that observable rather than merely asserting it, because CONFIRMI is supplied blank: had the task continued, the WHEN SPACES arm at :175-181 would have reported 'Confirm to add this transaction...' and moved -1 into CONFIRML. Exactly one message is reported and it is the Merchant Zip one; the cursor is on MZIPL and on nothing else; expectedWrites is empty and TRANSACT still holds its three seeded rows byte for byte, which is the positive form of 'this path writes nothing'. TRANSACT has no REWRITE and no DELETE anywhere in the program, and the only EXEC CICS WRITE is the one at :713 that this path never reaches. THE MESSAGE ON TWO CHANNELS, AND THE TWO BYTES BETWEEN THEM. The text is one literal but it is observable at two widths, so it is pinned at both: WS-MESSAGE is PIC X(80) at :38 and ERRMSGO is PIC X(78) in app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY, and MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :520 moves eighty characters into a seventy-eight character receiver. Both are left justified and space padded, which is what a MOVE into an alphanumeric receiver does (rule R5), and reporting only one of them would make that two-byte loss unobservable. THE CURSOR IS METADATA, NOT PAYLOAD. MZIPL is an xxxL item - a COMP PIC S9(4) length item - so it carries the cursor request rather than a screen value, and it is declared as this response's cursorField instead of as a member of the sent payload. The arithmetic of the symbolic map is what makes that split concrete rather than stylistic (practice B11): COTRN2AI images 555 bytes, of which the 21 xxxI payload items occupy 396 - 4+40+8+8+40+8 for the header six, then 11+16 for the two keys, 2+4+10+60+12+10+10 for the seven detail fields, 9+30+25+10 for the four merchant fields, 1 for the confirmation and 78 for the error line - while the other 159 are the 12-byte TIOAPFX filler plus seven bytes of metadata per field, being a two-byte xxxL length item, a one-byte xxxF flag with its xxxA attribute redefinition, and a four-byte filler. Twenty-one times seven is 147, and 12 + 147 + 396 is 555. Not one of those 159 metadata bytes is a payload field, which is why this case names 21 output items and pins the cursor separately. No other xxxL item holds -1 on this path: the only MOVE -1 executed is the one at :316, since :123 belongs to the first-entry branch this re-entry does not take and every other cursor request sits in a guard that did not fire. THE HEADER, PINNED TO ONE INSTANT (practice B7). POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :552-571 moves CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02 from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy into TITLE01O and TITLE02O at their declared PIC X(40), WS-TRANID 'CT02' into TRNNAMEO, WS-PGMNAME 'COTRN02C' into PGMNAMEO, and then builds CURDATEO as MM/DD/YY and CURTIMEO as HH:MM:SS from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34 - the single instant all twenty cases in this folder use - so those two items are comparable byte for byte and the run is reproducible in any timezone. STATELESSNESS (rule R6, gates G37 and G38). All 22 fields of the 218-byte area are pinned and none omitted, because the conversation state travels in the payload rather than in a server-side session and an unpinned field is a field nobody has checked. The area is 218 bytes because app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy declares CARDDEMO-COMMAREA as 4+8+4+8+8+1+1+9+25+25+25+11+1+16+7+7 = 160 and COTRN02C extends the same 01 group at :72-80 with CDEMO-CT02-INFO as 16+16+8+1+1+16 = 58; in Java the extension stays a separate DTO field rather than widening the NavigationContext all seventeen online programs share, so the case declares one flat commarea map and the two layouts each take the names they own (practice B11). CDEMO-ACCT-ID and CDEMO-CARD-NUM stay at zeros even though this run resolved both: the program moves the resolved identifiers into the SCREEN fields at :221 and :223 and never into the communication area, and inventing a carry-forward it does not perform would be a behaviour change. G38 is satisfied by the state rather than by a highlight - this is the REENTER path, the error flag is raised and a cursor is requested - and no field is coloured, because COTRN02C copies no CSSETATY and assigns exactly one attribute byte anywhere: MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC at :727, on the successful-write arm only. This is a rejecting path, so ERRMSGC is pinned at its default colour instead. DEAD DECLARATIONS PRESERVED, NOT TIDIED (practice B5). WS-ACCTDAT-FILE PIC X(08) VALUE 'ACCTDAT ' is declared at :40 and COPY CVACT01Y at :89, and neither is referenced anywhere in the program's 783 lines - no DATASET operand names WS-ACCTDAT-FILE and no field of ACCOUNT-RECORD is ever moved. That is why resolving an account identifier here does NOT read the account master: :223 moves eleven digits from the cross-reference record into a screen field and stops. No ACCTDAT input is declared by this case and no ACCTDAT row appears in any of its expectations - seeding a master the program never opens would assert a read that does not exist - and no case in this folder may declare one either. The deadness is asserted as the non-event it is, by COTRN02CParityTest.DeadDeclarations. THE TWO DATASETS THIS CASE SEEDS. CCXREF is seeded from the first five rows of cardxref.txt exactly as they ship, 36 bytes wide, and is deliberately NOT pre-padded: app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares CARD-XREF-RECORD as XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) + XREF-CUST-ID 9(09) + XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) + FILLER X(14), which is 16+9+11+14 = 50, the fixture omits that trailing FILLER so its rows measure 16+9+11 = 36, and the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation declared below supplies the fourteen spaces once, at seed time, as the sole owner of that repair (gate G16, risk R-F). CXACAIX is not seeded as a dataset of its own (gate G45), no tenth fixture is named - the set is closed at the nine derived from app/data/ASCII - and every dataset is addressed by its application.yml binding key rather than by name, so not one fully-qualified mainframe dataset name appears anywhere in this file - not in an input, not in an expectation and not in this prose (gate G46). Three TRANSACT rows are declared inline because no ASCII fixture ships for that master, which is populated online rather than loaded; each is 350 bytes summed from app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy as 16+2+4+10+100+11+9+50+50+10+16+26+26+20 with the trailing FILLER X(20) present and space-filled (gates G19 and G21), and all three are the same rows the sibling cases seed. The code page is stated as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default (practice B8). CASE ALLOCATION, RECONCILED IN THE OPEN (practice B4). This slot previously held the card arm's class-test rejection - a CARDNINI of '1.2.3' reported as 'Card Number must be Numeric...' at :212-216 - and that behaviour is not lost by this case taking the slot: TransactionViewControllerTest.aPartFilledCardNumberIsNonNumeric and its fully non-numeric sibling both assert that literal directly, each with verifyNoInteractions on the cross-reference so the skipped conversion is asserted too, and case08 pins the account arm's matching literal 'Account ID must be Numeric...' as a full parity case. What this case contributes instead exists nowhere else in the folder: the base cluster's NORMAL arm, the sixteen-digit renormalisation, the ACTIDIN overwrite from a non-first fixture row, and the eleventh arm of the cascade, all judged as bytes across the screen, the communication area, both message channels and the master's final state. The reallocation is recorded here rather than made silently, and nothing is renamed. BASELINE PROVENANCE (practice B12). Every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - by structured reading of MAIN-PARA, PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS, READ-CCXREF-FILE, VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS, SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN and POPULATE-HEADER-INFO, cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts (CVACT03Y at 50 with 36 supplied, CVTRA05Y at 350, COCOM01Y at 160 plus the 58-byte CT02 extension), against the xxxI and xxxO widths of app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY, and against the real bytes of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt, whose second row was sliced at the copybook's own offsets to obtain both the key and the account it resolves to. It was NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution: running the legacy programs is empirically impossible in this environment, which Agent Action Plan section 0.7.6 establishes with eight independently verified blockers - among them a compiler whose indexed-file handler is disabled, the absence of any CICS emulator, and the absence of the IBM-supplied DFHAID and DFHBMSCA copybooks this program copies at :92-93, which is why the AID below is named by mnemonic through common.CicsAid (risk R-D) - and the change of provenance is escalated as risk R-A rather than absorbed silently. NO USER RULES EXIST: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided', and that line is the whole document, so no rule forces this file into scope and no rule constrains how it is written. The absence is stated explicitly and is not treated as permission to lower the bar: the standard held here is the Agent Action Plan section 0.10.2 enterprise practices, cited by name where they bite - B1 (every literal derived and verified against the fixture bytes or a PICTURE clause, no placeholder anywhere), B3 (the reference trees app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms, app/csd and app/data are read-only and were not touched), B4 (the R-B inversion, the corrected sibling owners and the case reallocation all disclosed), B5 (the dead ACCTDAT declaration preserved, the renormalisation and the overwrite reproduced exactly as written, the eleven-arm order neither reordered nor collapsed), B7 (a pinned clock), B8 (binding keys, a named code page, explicit literals and the ten populated fields stated at full width), B11 (every width summed from a PICTURE clause) and B12 (the provenance statement above). GATES DISCHARGED: G15 (one of exactly twenty cases in parity/COTRN02C), G16 (the cardxref seed stays 36 bytes and is normalised at seed time, never pre-padded), G18 (the diff count must be zero, per module rather than per build), G19 and G21 (350-byte records whose FILLER is present and space-filled), G30 (the three-arm RESP EVALUATE in source order and the eleven-arm cascade reaching its final arm), G37 (no server-side session state - the whole 218-byte area travels in the payload), G38 (the REENTER state with the error flag raised and the cursor requested, and no highlight because this screen has none), G45 (the base cluster keyed on XREF-CARD-NUM here and the CXACAIX alternate index keyed on XREF-ACCT-ID elsewhere, over one seeded dataset), G46 (binding keys, never a dataset-name literal), G47 (the cross-reference read's NORMAL outcome, with its NOTFND and WHEN OTHER siblings named and owned) and G51 (the controller is driven as a plain object - no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container and no HTTP in the path). DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED, because COTRN02C has none of them: G32 (zero GO TO, so no backward jump to restructure), G35 (zero CALL 'CEE3ABD', which is why the return code is 0 and no abend path exists), G39 (no pagination loop), G40 (no XCTL on this path, so no nextProgram naming another program - the response names COTRN02C itself, because the RETURN at :530 continues the pseudo-conversation) and G43 (no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC).
